clinician.final_diagnosis: Inflammatory Myofibroblastic Tumor (IMT) of the cecum
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 68-year-old man presented with one month of right lower quadrant colicky pain radiating to the back, associated with 2-3 kg weight loss and anorexia. Physical examination revealed right lower quadrant tenderness without rebound, with normal vital signs. CT imaging identified a well-demarcated homogenous solitary mass in the cecum with thickened ileal wall. Colonoscopy confirmed a large mass-like lesion in the cecum, and biopsy was obtained. Pathology demonstrated lamina propria infiltration by polymorphonuclear cells and eosinophils with immunohistochemical profile positive for vimentin and CD68, focally positive for ALK, CD34, and smooth muscle actin, and negative for C-Kit, desmin, and pancytokeratin—findings consistent with inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor. The patient underwent right hemicolectomy with ileocolic anastomosis; intraoperative findings included approximately 40 mL ascites and ileocolic intussusception. The diagnosis of IMT was confirmed by pathology, and the patient was referred for surgical resection, which was successfully completed.
